description: What an HTML email owes, which is almost none of what a page owes. A mail client renders static markup with inline styles: it runs no script, resolves no stylesheet, and has no pointer, focus model, viewport or scroll container. Outlook renders through the Word engine, Gmail strips a great deal on the way in, and a large share of readers see the message with images switched off before they see anything else. So the rules that govern a page are not softened here, they are replaced. Every gate below is one a regex can settle, because a gate with nothing behind it reads in a report exactly like a rule that held.

gates.title: Layout Is Tables
gates.rule: The layout is nested tables. Flexbox and grid are unreliable in Outlook, which renders through the Word engine, so a layout built on them collapses for a large share of business readers.

check.message: no table found - email layout is nested tables, not flex or grid

gates.fix: Move the layout onto nested tables and put every declaration inline on the cell it governs.

gates.title: No Stylesheet, Script, Or Font Host
gates.rule: A style block, a link element, a script, or an import from a font host. Every one is stripped or ignored, and a message that fetches a font announces itself as a campaign before it is read.

check.message: a mail client resolves none of these

gates.fix: Delete them and name a system font stack inline on each cell.

gates.title: No SVG
gates.rule: Gmail strips SVG outright and Outlook will not draw it. Anything vector is either a raster served over https or is drawn with cell borders, background colours, and border-radius.

check.message: SVG does not render in Gmail or Outlook

gates.fix: Rasterise the mark to PNG at twice its displayed size, or draw the shape with table cells.

gates.title: Every Image Declares Its Width
gates.rule: An explicit width attribute on the tag, so the layout holds while images load and when they never do. Outlook blocks images by default, and a box with no declared size collapses to nothing.

check.message: an img with no width attribute collapses when images are blocked

gates.fix: Add width and height attributes to every img, and serve the file at twice its displayed size.

gates.title: Every Image Carries Alt Text
gates.rule: Alt text saying what the image shows, because for a reader with images off it is the image. A missing alt leaves a blank where the proof was.

check.message: an img with no alt is a blank space for every reader with images off

gates.fix: Add descriptive alt text to every img, naming what it shows rather than the file.

gates.title: No Tracking Pixel
gates.rule: A one-by-one image whose only job is to report an open. Filters read it as a campaign marker, the privacy proxies most readers now sit behind strip it, and what it reports is wrong often enough not to be worth the cost.

check.message: a tracking pixel is read as a campaign marker and reports badly anyway

gates.fix: Delete it. Measure replies and visits instead.

gates.title: The Link Is Its Own Destination
gates.rule: Every href is the full URL it goes to. A shortener hides the destination from the reader and from the filter, and both treat that as what it is.

check.message: a shortened link hides its destination from the reader and the filter

gates.fix: Replace the shortened link with the destination it points at.

gates.title: A One-Click Unsubscribe
gates.rule: The List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers, so a mailbox provider can offer its own control beside the sender's name. Asking somebody to compose a reply is friction they will not accept, and providers now expect the headers from anything sending at volume.

check.message: no List-Unsubscribe header is set on the send

gates.fix: Add the token-based endpoint, put the link in both halves, and set both headers on every send.

gates.title: A Plain-Text Half
gates.rule: The message goes as multipart with a text alternative, built from the same content so the two cannot drift. A message with no text half is one a filter scores worse and some readers never see.

check.message: no plain-text alternative is built beside the HTML

gates.fix: Render both halves from the same paragraphs and pass both to the transport.

gates.title: The Postal Address Is Carried
gates.rule: Commercial email is required to carry a physical postal address, and a footer that names only a brand is one a reader cannot answer and a regulator can act on.

check.message: no postal address reaches the footer

gates.fix: Put the postal line in the footer of both halves, read from configuration rather than typed in.

gates.title: The Sheet Goes Fluid
gates.rule: A fixed sheet width with a max-width beside it, so the message holds its column on a desktop and fills the screen on a phone. A fixed width alone is a horizontal scroll for most of the people who open it.

check.message: no max-width on the sheet, so it cannot go fluid on a phone

gates.fix: Give the outer table a fixed width and a max-width, and let the cells inside it size to their content.

gates.title: Grounds Are Declared, Not Inherited
gates.rule: Mail clients apply their own dark mode by inverting light grounds and leaving dark ones alone. A cell with no declared background is the one that comes out wrong, so bgcolor sits beside every background-color.

check.message: no bgcolor attribute, so a client's dark mode decides the grounds

gates.fix: Set bgcolor and background-color on every band and every nested cell that sits on a ground of its own.
